result.summary: Excludes private broadcast connections from standard peer discouragement handling on the 31.x release branch. Misbehaving private broadcast peers are still disconnected, but their addresses are not added to the discouragement filter.
result.problem: Discouraging private broadcast peers alters observable network state, which could allow external observers or peers to detect or deanonymize private broadcast connections.
evidence: PR description: "Discouraging a private broadcast connection may be observable. Prevent this by keeping private broadcast connections outside normal discouragement handling. Misbehaving private broadcast peers are still disconnected."
Commit 22ac577566: "Keep private broadcast connections outside normal discouragement handling. Misbehaving private broadcast peers are still disconnected."
result.scope_notes: Backport to the 31.x branch; the patch for #36312 could not be applied cleanly and was rebased.
result.card: Excludes private broadcast connections from normal P2P address discouragement on the 31.x release branch while still disconnecting them on misbehavior. The change prevents observable discouragement state from deanonymizing or leaking private broadcast activity. This backport re-applies changes from PR #36312.
uncertainties: The diff was not provided, preventing direct inspection of the 4 modified files.

risk.why: Alters peer disconnection and discouragement logic in P2P networking, where a bug could allow misbehaving peers to repeatedly reconnect or degrade node resources.
